# Quadratics — summary

| Need | Formula / method |
|---|---|
| Axis of symmetry 📘 | $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$ |
| Vertex | $h = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$, $k = f(h)$ |
| Vertex form 🧠 | $a(x - h)^2 + k$ → vertex $(h,\ k)$ |
| Factorised form 🧠 | $a(x - p)(x - q)$ → roots $p$, $q$ |
| Quadratic formula 📘 | $x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ |
| Discriminant 📘 | $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac$ |

**Nature of roots 🧠:** $\Delta > 0$ two distinct · $\Delta = 0$ two equal · $\Delta < 0$ none · "real roots" $\Delta \geq 0$.

**Tangent line to a parabola:** equate, rearrange to $= 0$, set $\Delta = 0$.

**Inequalities:** find the roots, sketch, read where the graph is above / below the $x$-axis. For $a > 0$: "$< 0$" between the roots, "$> 0$" outside.

**Applications:** max / min → vertex; "when" → solve; "for which values" → inequality. Check the context (e.g. $t \geq 0$).

**Watch out:** vertex sign in $(x + 3)^2$ → $h = -3$ · $a \neq 0$ when $k$ multiplies $x^2$ · $(-3)^2 = 9$.
